summary:
TerraShield AI is an AI-assisted environmental monitoring dashboard for Kerala. It brings three NASA-based data streams into one visual interface: rainfall (FloodSense, from GPM precipitation data), land-surface temperature (from MODIS), and ocean health (OceanGuard). Users can explore monthly time series, spot unusual rainfall months, view a rainfall-based flood-risk indicator, and run trend tests that report slope and statistical significance. Ocean observations are classified as normal, moderate-change or high-change. A CSV upload feature lets users analyse their own environmental datasets in the same way.

The project addresses the challenge by turning raw, scattered environmental data into signals people can read quickly, using charts, anomaly markers, trend statistics and simple indicators. In the demo, rainfall showed no statistically significant trend (p = 0.073), while temperature showed a significant decreasing trend (p = 0.0011).

This matters because Kerala is vulnerable to floods and climate variability, and clearer historical patterns help people understand and communicate environmental change. TerraShield is an exploratory analysis tool, not an official warning service, so its risk indicators should be checked against authoritative local alerts.
details:
TerraShield AI is a single dashboard that combines three environmental signals for Kerala:

  • FloodSense (rainfall): Shows 141 months of NASA GPM precipitation data as a time series. It highlights unusual rainfall months (2 in the demo) and shows a rainfall-based flood-risk indicator (latest alert: Low, 0.241 mm/hr).
  • Temperature: Plots NASA MODIS land-surface temperature (min 23.11 °C, max 29.68 °C, average 26.43 °C) and runs a linear trend test.
  • OceanGuard (ocean health): Classifies monthly ocean observations as normal, moderate-change or high-change (7 / 2 / 1 in the demo).

For each trend, the dashboard reports the slope, the p-value and whether the result is statistically significant at the 0.05 threshold. Users can also upload their own CSV of environmental observations and explore it with the same charts and summaries.

Benefits

  • Puts rainfall, temperature and ocean data in one place instead of several separate sources.
  • Makes patterns easier to see and explain, using seasonal peaks, anomaly markers and plain-language indicators.
  • Reports whether a trend is statistically significant, so users don’t over-read noise. In the demo, rainfall showed no significant trend (p = 0.073), while temperature showed a significant decreasing trend (p = 0.0011).
  • The CSV upload makes it reusable with other datasets.

Intended impact

TerraShield AI aims to make historical environmental data easier for students, researchers and local communities to understand and communicate. It is meant to support awareness of flood risk and climate variability in Kerala, a region exposed to heavy monsoon rainfall and a long coastline. It is not an official emergency-warning system, and its risk indicators should be checked against authoritative local alerts.

Tools and technologies

  • Data: NASA GPM (rainfall) and NASA MODIS (land-surface temperature)
  • Analysis: Linear trend testing (slope and p-value), anomaly detection, threshold-based classification

Creativity

  • It combines land, rainfall and ocean signals in one interface, rather than a single-purpose tool.
  • It pairs visuals with statistical tests, so it shows both what changed and whether the change is meaningful.
  • The modular branding (FloodSense, OceanGuard) gives each signal its own identity within one platform.
  • It is honest about its limits, with a clear note that it is exploratory and not a safety service.

Factors the team considered

  • Data reliability: Using established NASA sources and labelling them clearly.
  • Statistical honesty: Reporting p-values and stating when no significant trend is found.
  • Responsible use: Making clear that risk indicators are exploratory, to avoid false confidence in safety decisions.
  • Usability: Simple indicators and charts for non-experts.
  • Flexibility: CSV upload, so the tool isn’t limited to one dataset.
